Country A: 1 laptop costs 40/120 = 1/3 bicycle. Country B: 1 laptop costs 30/40 = 0.75 bicycle. A has the comparative advantage in laptops. B's cost of a bicycle is 4/3 laptops and A's is 3, so B has the comparative advantage in bicycles.

The new curve's horizontal intercept stays at 120 laptops, and its vertical intercept goes from 40 to 80 bicycles.

Trade terms between 1/3 and 3/4 bicycle per laptop work.

answers.brief_reasoning: 40 bicycles / 120 laptops = 1/3 bicycle per laptop
answers.final_answer: 1/3 bicycle per laptop (40/120)

answers.brief_reasoning: A's cost is 1/3 bicycle, which is lower than B's 0.75 bicycle
answers.final_answer: Country A

answers.brief_reasoning: Draw a straight-line PPC from (0 laptops, 40 bicycles) to (120 laptops, 0 bicycles). The new curve, PPC2, pivots outward along the bicycle axis to 80 bicycles and keeps the laptop intercept at 120.
answers.final_answer: Original PPC: intercepts at 40 bicycles and 120 laptops. New PPC2: intercepts at 80 bicycles and 120 laptops (it rotates outward on the bicycle axis).

answers.brief_reasoning: Specialization by comparative advantage, then trade at terms between the two countries' opportunity costs
answers.final_answer: Country A specializes in laptops and Country B specializes in bicycles. They trade at terms between 1/3 and 3/4 bicycle per laptop (for example, 1 laptop for 1/2 bicycle). Each country then gets goods at a lower cost than producing them itself, so each can consume beyond its own PPC.
